issue.body:
It appears that windows OpenSSH cannot cope with single quoted strings. Use double-quotes instead.

Fix #10813

body: The single quotes should not be being passed to Gitea AFAICS it's probably something to do with the shell.

> The single quotes should not be being passed to Gitea AFAICS it's probably something to do with the shell.

No it's nothing to do with the shell. On Windows, the command line is passed to each program as a string. Each executable parses its own command line. On Windows, single quotes are by convention not supported, only double quotes. Go follows this convention. Therefore, passing single quotes to the gitea command line on Windows won't work.

IMO this is a bug not a feature enhancement. The authorized_keys generated by gitea on Windows, is incompatible with command line parsing on Windows, and won't work.

issue.title: Failed to get repository owner (user): no such table: user

repository.name: gogs
repository.description: Gogs is a painless self-hosted Git service

issue.body:
First of all, I like gogs very much! Thank you for your effort :+1: 

For the last hour I've been struggling with the following error:

```
/tmp ➜ git clone git@myhost.mydomain:robin/documents.git
Cloning into 'documents'...
Gogs: Internal error
Failed to get repository owner (robin): no such table: user
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.

Please make sure you have the correct access rights
and the repository exists.
```

My `app.ini` looked like this (shortened):

```
...
[database]
DB_TYPE = sqlite3
PATH = data/gogs.db

[repository]
ROOT = /var/repositories
...
```

Gogs lives in `/opt/gogs` and the SQLite database was created in `/var/repositories/data/gogs.db`. Somehow when I try to clone a repo, gogs looks up the user in `/opt/gogs/data/gogs.db` instead of `/var/repositories/data/gogs.db`.

When I change `PATH = data/gogs.db` to `PATH = /var/repositories/data/gogs.db` (and restart gogs) it **works**.

Maybe it's not an issue, but I had to debug gogs to figure this out. Probably a hint about this should be added to the documentation?

issue.body:
Properly handle spaces in AppPath and CustomConf within hooks and
authorized_keys. Unfortunately here we don't seem to be able to get away
with using go-shellquote as it appears that Windows doesn't play too
well with singlequote quoting - therefore we will avoid singlequote
quoting unless we absolutely cannot get away without it, e.g. \n or !.

Fix #10813

Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>
